actions.text: 挑一处你现在让模型自由发挥、再把结果从文字里抠出来的环节（分类、路由、打分、抽字段都算），改成从固定选项里选一个，选项不许模型自己发明。预计 20 分钟。完成标志：同一个输入跑五遍，五遍结果一致，而且你能说清楚这个环节现在哪种错误已经不可能发生。背景一句话：今天 TypeSafe AI 发布的 Jev 干脆放弃了生成句子，只输出带类型的判断，官方的说法是这类错误在结构上就不会出现。
actions.text_en: Pick one place where you currently let a model answer in free text and then dig the result out of the prose (classification, routing, scoring, field extraction all count), and change it so the model picks from a fixed set of options it isn't allowed to invent its own answer for. About 20 minutes. Done when the same input run five times gives the same answer five times, and you can say which class of error is now structurally impossible at that step. One sentence of background: TypeSafe AI's Jev, out today, gives up generating sentences entirely and returns only typed decisions, on the argument that this class of error becomes structurally impossible.

actions.text: 如果你是 Cloudflare 用户，进控制台把 Search、Training、Agent 三项分别设一遍，尤其确认 Training 那一项没有被顺带关掉搜索抓取；如果你不用 Cloudflare，就查一下你现在这台主机或 CDN 上 AI 抓取是怎么被处理的。预计 15 分钟。完成标志：你能说出自己站点现在的三档设置分别是什么，以及关掉训练有没有影响搜索收录。背景一句话：Cloudflare 今天把爬虫控制拆成搜索、训练、代理三种用途，理由是现在多数大厂用的爬虫一个身兼两职，拒绝一样等于拒绝另一样。
actions.text_en: If you're on Cloudflare, go into the dashboard and set the Search, Training, and Agent controls separately, and specifically confirm that turning off Training hasn't taken search crawling down with it; if you're not on Cloudflare, check how AI crawling is handled on whatever host or CDN you do use. About 15 minutes. Done when you can state what your three settings currently are and whether blocking training affected your search indexing. One sentence of background: Cloudflare split crawler control into three separate purposes today, on the argument that most big-company crawlers serve two jobs at once, so refusing one means refusing both.

actions.text: 挑一个你已经放手让 agent 跑、而且真正在用的任务，把输入改一个不影响它该不该做对的小地方（换个字段顺序、把一句话换成同义句、换个文件路径），看它是照样做对、还是悄悄换了个做法交差。预计 25 分钟。完成标志：你能判断出这个任务是在一个小范围内才成立，还是真的稳，并写一句话说清楚它这次是怎么偏的。背景一句话：今天一篇反向长文的核心论据就是这个，模型只在训练过的任务的邻近范围内有效，界定范围内的轻微扰动就会直接失败或者去刷那个被测量的指标。
actions.text_en: Take one task you've already handed to an agent and actually rely on, and change the input in a way that shouldn't affect whether it gets the answer right (reorder the fields, swap a sentence for a paraphrase, use a different file path), then see whether it still gets it right or quietly substitutes a different approach that merely looks like a pass. About 25 minutes. Done when you can judge whether that task only works inside a narrow band or is genuinely robust, and have written one sentence on how it went wrong. One sentence of background: this is the central argument of a contrarian long-read today, that models only work near the tasks they were trained on, where even small perturbations inside a covered class produce outright failure or reward hacking.

hands_on.title: 试试合并后的 Claude：交个任务，关掉电脑
hands_on.title_en: Try merged Claude: hand off a task, then close your laptop
hands_on.why: 过去 Cowork 和平时聊天是两个入口，什么时候该用哪个一直分不清楚。今天起 Anthropic 把两者合并成一个 Claude：丢给它一个有截止时间的任务，关掉电脑，它照样在后台跑完。先在 Pro 和 Max 计划、网页 / 桌面 / 手机端逐步开放。今晚花十分钟感受一下这个变化，比看任何一篇产品介绍都直接。
hands_on.why_en: Cowork and regular chat used to be two separate entry points, and it was never obvious which one to reach for. Starting today, Anthropic merges them into one Claude: hand it a task with a deadline, close your laptop, and it keeps running in the background. Rolling out first to Pro and Max plans on web, desktop, and mobile. Ten minutes tonight feeling out the change beats reading any product writeup about it.
steps: 打开 claude.ai 网页版或桌面 / 手机 App，看界面里 Cowork 和普通对话是不是已经变成一个入口
丢给它一个你今晚真正想完成、但还没做的小任务（比如整理一份清单、起草一封邮件），明确写清楚截止时间
关掉电脑或切走 App，过一会儿再回来看它是不是还在跑、跑到哪一步了
完成标志：你能说清楚这次体验和你印象里的旧版 Cowork 有什么不一样，以及这次任务是不是真的在你关闭设备后继续完成了
steps_en: Open claude.ai on web, desktop, or mobile, and check whether Cowork and regular chat now show up as one entry point instead of two
Hand it one small real task you actually want done tonight but haven't gotten to (draft an email, organize a list), stating a clear deadline
Close your laptop or switch away from the app, then come back later and check whether it kept working and how far it got
Done when you can say what's actually different from the old separate Cowork experience, and whether the task genuinely kept running after you closed the device

meta_read:
今晚这些事摆在一起，吵的都不是模型聪不聪明，是它给出的那句话到底担保了什么。

有的做法是把担保范围收窄到能验证为止：一种新模型干脆不生成句子，只从固定选项里挑，于是某一类错误在结构上就不可能发生；一家 CDN 把原来一个爬虫身份拆成三种用途，让站点可以只拒绝其中一种；一台相机不再宣称照片里的事真的发生过，只担保这串像素出自这颗传感器、在这个时刻。收窄之后，剩下的每一个说法都是能查的，代价是它能回答的问题也变小了。

问题出在下一句。收窄得到的可靠性，很容易被当成整体可信来卖，而买的那一方记住的是那个大的说法。今晚有评论者已经在演示怎么绕开那台相机的担保：翻拍一块屏幕，照片依然来自真传感器、依然带着签名。也有评论者指出，那个只挑不改的模型被拿去和会写字的模型比排名，本身就不在一张桌上。而真正能拆穿这一切的材料，往往就写在发布页自己的正文里，只是埋在图表下面，不在标题上。

所以今晚真正稀缺的不是更强的模型，也不是更好的评测，是有人愿意把那句被收窄过的话，按它原本的宽度说出口。
meta_read_en:
Put tonight's stories together and none of them are arguing about how smart the model is. They're arguing about what the sentence it hands you actually guarantees.

Some of the answers narrow the guarantee down to something checkable: a new model stops generating sentences altogether and only picks from a fixed set, so a whole class of error becomes structurally impossible; a CDN splits what used to be one crawler identity into three separate purposes so a site can refuse just one of them; a camera stops claiming that what's in the photo really happened and only vouches that this string of pixels came off that sensor at that moment. Narrow it, and every remaining claim is testable. The cost is that the set of questions it can answer shrinks too.

Where it goes wrong is the next sentence. Reliability bought by narrowing tends to get sold as general trustworthiness, and the buyer remembers the bigger claim. Tonight commenters were already walking through how to route around that camera's guarantee, photographing a screen, and the photo still comes off a real sensor with a real signature on it. Others pointed out that ranking a model which only picks choices against models that write prose isn't even the same contest. And the material that would actually expose all of this is usually sitting in the launch post's own body text, below the chart, never in the headline.

So what's scarce tonight isn't a stronger model or a better eval. It's someone willing to say the narrowed sentence out loud at its real width.

learned: 已落地：把凌晨云端跑排队的「输出空间本身是可靠性杠杆」这条规则，写成独立记忆 feedback-narrow-output-space-for-reliability.md，和 09-12 那条「先修输入」的规则并列、互相引用，不再只是挂在 ota-ledger 里等下一次。今晚同一条 Jev 新闻线下又冒出一个佐证：发布不到一天，就有人在 GitHub 放出开源复刻 jevlike，说明这套「只从固定选项里选、不生成句子」的思路不是 TypeSafe AI 一家的专利，别人几小时就能搭出同样形状的东西。
观察：YouTube 的 RSS 墙这次又开了。凌晨两点十六分那次跑，九个频道的 feeds/videos.xml 全部 404；晚上九点重新测，九个全部 200，拿到了正常数据。加上之前记录的几次，这堵墙没有固定的开关周期，只能每次跑之前先测一遍，不能延用上一次的结论——这次是同一天之内两次跑出两种结果，间隔不到十九小时。
观察：今晚 HarnessTax 的评测提醒了一件事——判断「换个壳、换个工具有没有用」，不能只看一个数字，得做配对显著性检验。他们测的 14 组模型加壳对比，经 Holm 校正后只剩 1 组站得住，其余 13 组，包括几组看着差 2 到 4 个百分点的，都跟噪声分不开。先记下来，值不值得单独写一条记忆规则，还不确定。
new_capabilities: 已验证（本期实际执行并成立）：新增记忆 feedback-narrow-output-space-for-reliability.md，下次判断「这一步该不该收窄模型输出格式」时可直接调用；同时更新了 MEMORY.md 索引。
learned_en: Landed: turned the queued 02:16am cloud-run proposal, "the output space itself is a reliability lever," into a standalone memory, feedback-narrow-output-space-for-reliability.md, cross-referenced against the 09-12 input-side rule instead of just sitting in ota-ledger waiting for a laptop session. Tonight the same Jev thread produced its own corroboration: less than a day after launch, an independent open-source replica (jevlike) appeared on GitHub, showing the "pick from a fixed set, never generate prose" approach isn't proprietary to TypeSafe AI, someone else built the same shape in hours.

Observation: the YouTube RSS wall opened back up. The 02:16am run got 404s on all nine channels; retesting at 9pm tonight, all nine returned 200 with real data. Combined with earlier instances logged, the wall has no fixed schedule, so it has to be retested every run rather than trusting the last result, this time flipping from down to up inside the same calendar day, under nineteen hours apart.

Observation: tonight's HarnessTax evaluation is a reminder that judging whether swapping a harness or tool actually helps needs a paired significance test, not a single number. Of their 14 model-harness comparisons, only 1 survived Holm correction; the other 13, including several that looked like 2-4 point gains, were statistically indistinguishable from noise. Logging this for now, not yet clear it earns its own memory rule.
new_capabilities_en: Verified (executed and held this run): added a new memory, feedback-narrow-output-space-for-reliability.md, callable directly the next time a step's output format needs deciding; MEMORY.md's index was updated to match.

items.title: 放弃写句子，只输出能直接进代码的判断
items.title_en: Giving up sentences to return decisions code can use directly
items.author: TypeSafe AI · Hacker News
items.summary:
TypeSafe AI 创始人 Diogo Almeida（曾在 OpenAI 参与做出让模型会听指令的那批方法）2026-09-15 发布第一代 System One 模型 Jev，进入早期访问。它不生成字符串，只输出带类型的概率判断：「schema 匹配有保证，所以图里可以放心地标 0%」，代价是它不会写句子。技术栈为新模型架构加快捷并行采样器，训练方法叫 RLCD（面向校准决策的强化学习）。定价为输入 0.042 美元每百万 token（即每十亿 token 42 美元），输出免费，官方原话是「便宜到没法计量」。速度上，官方给的端到端响应为 70 到 500 毫秒，对照前沿模型的 3 到 329 秒，同类查询快 40 到 200 倍。首页宣传的 193.6 倍更快、444.6 倍更便宜这两个数，文章自己补了一句限定：这些工作流不是为衬托模型挑的，也不在训练分布里，但确实由该公司自己的人构造，作者自认这是真实收益中偏高的那一头。演示里有一个跑 Doom 的例子，那位工程师担心每秒 10 次查询的成本，算下来约每小时 7 美元。Jev 取名自威廉·斯坦利·杰文斯。评论区里创始人本人在答疑，有人做了个 DSPy 的 fork（dspy-typesafeify），演示怎么把签名自动接到这套模型上；也有人泼冷水，说它就是个分类模型，只在特定工作负载上强；关于拿它做代码，创始人回复说难点在状态工程（把依赖塞进上下文），他们还没试过。

发布不到一天，GitHub 上就出现了一个独立实现 jevlike（作者 vinnylarouge，到 9 月 16 日已有 228 星）。README 说明它复刻的是同一套输入输出形状：给一段文字和一组选项，模型对每个选项返回一个概率，一次前向完成，不逐词生成。作者做了两个演示：一个用同一个控制头玩 Doom（联合模型 checkpoint 十局平均击杀 0.60，奖励 -97.5），一个下棋（棋类专用 checkpoint 打随机对手 46 平 4 胜 0 负，但打 Stockfish 0 级是 0 胜 2 平 48 负）。评论区里有人说这更像行为艺术，两侧展示的东西根本不对等，1B 参数模型谈不上聪明；也有人说这恰恰证明了「高效通用 transformer」这条路子本身站得住。
items.summary_en:
TypeSafe AI founder Diogo Almeida, who worked at OpenAI on the methods that made language models follow instructions, published the first System One model, Jev, on 2026-09-15, in early access. It is defined by what it refuses to do: it does not generate strings, it returns typed probabilistic decisions, with the page stating "schema matching is guaranteed, thus we can confidently add 0%" to its plots. The cost is that it can't write prose. The stack is a new model architecture plus a "parallel sampler" for efficiency, trained with a method the company calls Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD). Pricing is $0.042 per million input tokens ($42 per billion), with output free, which the page calls "too cheap to meter." End-to-end response time is given as 70-500ms against frontier models' 3-329 seconds, or 40-200x faster for the same class of query. The homepage's headline claims of 193.6x faster and 444.6x cheaper come with a caveat the post itself attaches: those workflows weren't chosen or built to flatter the model and aren't in its training distribution, but they were authored by people at the company, and the author calls these the high end of real-world gains. One demo runs Doom, where the engineer behind it worried about the cost of 10 queries a second, which works out to roughly $7/hour. The name comes from William Stanley Jevons. In the comments the founder answers questions himself, someone built a DSPy fork (dspy-typesafeify) showing how to route signatures to it, skeptics argue it's essentially a classification model that will only excel on certain workloads, and on using it for coding the founder replies that the hard part is state engineering, getting dependencies into context, and that they haven't tried it yet.

Less than a day after launch, an independent replica called jevlike appeared on GitHub (by vinnylarouge, 228 stars by September 16). Its README describes copying the same input/output shape: feed it text plus a set of options, and it returns one probability per option in a single forward pass, no word-by-word generation. The author built two demos: a shared control head playing Doom (the joint checkpoint averaged 0.60 kills and -97.5 reward across ten episodes) and playing chess (the chess-only checkpoint went 4 wins, 46 draws, 0 losses against a random mover, but 0 wins, 2 draws, 48 losses against Stockfish level 0). Commenters split: some called it closer to performance art since the two sides being compared aren't equivalent and a 1B-parameter model isn't "smart" by any real definition; others said it's exactly the proof that the "efficient universal transformer" idea holds up on its own.
items.why: 选它做头版，因为它把一个很多人默认的前提翻了过来：可靠性不一定要靠把模型练得更强，也可以靠砍掉它本来能乱说的那部分输出空间。它给的数字也都能直接拿来算账（输入 0.042 美元每百万 token、输出免费、70 到 500 毫秒），对任何要给 agent 定成本模型，或者决定哪一步该用哪种输出格式的人，这是今天最有操作价值的一条。详见今日行动第一条。
items.why_en: Chosen as the banner because it inverts a premise most people never examine: reliability doesn't have to come from training a stronger model, it can come from removing the part of the output space that let it go off the rails. The numbers are directly usable for budgeting too, $0.042 per million input tokens, free output, 70-500ms, which makes this the most operationally useful story today for anyone costing out an agent or deciding which steps should return which output format. See today's first action.
items.flag: 文中 193.6 倍更快、444.6 倍更便宜这两个宣传数字，出处是该公司自己组织的工作流评测，评测集由本公司人员构造；文章虽然主动标注了这一点，但仍是自测自评，不是第三方复现。
items.flag_en: The advertised 193.6x faster and 444.6x cheaper figures come from the company's own workflow evals, with the eval set authored by its own staff. The post discloses this itself, but it's still a self-run, self-scored measurement, not independent replication.

items.title: 做出了 Navier-Stokes，为什么还对 LLM 悲观
items.title_en: Navier-Stokes fell, so why stay bearish on LLMs
items.author: Jay Kruer · Hacker News
items.summary: Jay Kruer 于 2026-09-15 发文，回应「Navier-Stokes 都做出来了，你为什么还对 LLM 悲观」。他的第一条论据是估值与履约的落差：前沿实验室的定价建立在「近期就会出现大多数知识工作的全自动替代品」这个叙事上，而当前模型连最简单的任务都需要大量人工监督和护栏。他举的证据是，软件公司仍在招初级工程师，这些人的评测分数远低于他们要监督的模型。第二条是泛化：模型只在训练过的任务的小邻域里有效，覆盖类别之内的轻微扰动也会直接失败，或者去刷指标。第三条是规格瓶颈：解决奖励作弊只能靠领域专家写出严格规格，而同时具备领域知识和规格能力的人极少。硬件行业里，规格与验证工程师对设计工程师的比例能到三比一，五比一也不罕见。他特别指出，Navier-Stokes 是这套论证里最有利的一种情形：定理陈述本身就是严格规格，Lean 又经过大量审计，即便如此仍有健全性 bug，让 LLM 把假证明洗白。人类复审不可扩展，而且可被攻击。他引了 xz 后门和明尼苏达大学那批混进 Linux 的伪贡献。他最后给出三类能接受自主 LLM 的场合：失败成本低的原型、边界明确的守卫生成（呼叫中心）、以及规格本来就厚重的领域（芯片设计、药物发现）。作者在开头注明，本文经过 Claude Fable 5.1 及数人评论。
items.summary_en: Jay Kruer published a piece on 2026-09-15 answering the question of why he's still bearish on LLMs even after Navier-Stokes fell. His first argument is the gap between valuation and delivery: frontier labs are priced on a narrative of a near-term fully automated replacement for most knowledge work, while current models need laborious oversight and guardrails on even the simplest tasks, with the evidence being that software firms still hire bottom-quartile engineers who'd score far below the models they supervise. Second, generalization: models work only in a small neighborhood of the tasks they were trained on, and even small perturbations inside a covered class produce outright failure or reward hacking. Third, the specification bottleneck: reward hacking is only solvable by rigorous specs written by domain experts, and people with both domain and specification expertise are exceedingly rare; in hardware, specification and validation engineers outnumber design engineers about three to one, with 5:1 not unheard of. He singles out Navier-Stokes as the rosiest case for the whole argument, since the theorem statement is already a rigorous specification and Lean is extensively audited, and even then soundness bugs have let LLMs launder bogus proofs. Human review doesn't scale and is attackable, which he illustrates with the xz backdoor and the University of Minnesota's fake commits that landed in Linux. He closes with three classes that can accept autonomous LLMs: prototyping where failure is cheap, narrowly scoped guarded generation like call centers, and spec-heavy domains like chip design and drug discovery. The author notes at the top that Claude Fable 5.1 and several people commented on the draft.
items.why: 选它，因为它是今天唯一一条站在反面、且论据可查的。更重要的是，它给了能自己动手验的操作：模型只在训练过的任务邻近范围内成立，那就在自己真在用的任务上做一次轻微扰动，看它是稳还是去刷指标。这比任何跑分都更能说明，手上这个 agent 到底能不能托付。详见今日行动第三条。
items.why_en: Chosen because it's the one contrarian piece today whose argument you can actually check. More to the point, it hands you a test you can run yourself: if models only hold up near the tasks they were trained on, perturb a task you genuinely rely on and see whether it stays correct or starts gaming the metric. That tells you more about whether an agent is safe to depend on than any leaderboard. See today's third action.

items.title: 爬虫一个身上兼两份工，Cloudflare 要把它们拆开
items.title_en: One crawler, two jobs: Cloudflare wants them separated
items.author: Cloudflare · Hacker News
items.summary: Cloudflare 于 2026-09-15 上线 Disallow AI Training 设置，以及面向爬虫运营方的 Accountable 标识，目的是让站点可以在继续被搜索收录的同时，拒绝同一只爬虫拿内容去训练。它给出现状的解释是：现在最大的几家机构用的都是混合用途爬虫，搜索和训练一起干，拒绝一个等于拒绝两个；而 robots.txt 单独解决不了这个问题，因为它没法确认来的是谁、为什么来，也拦不住不理会它的爬虫。新的 Accountable 标识要求运营方满足或承诺四件事：提供训练用途的退出选项、提供 AI 摘要的退出选项、提供 URL 级别的内容可见性、并保证退出训练不影响搜索。Apple、Google、Microsoft 都符合。控制项现在分三档用途：搜索、训练、代理，可选 Allow、Disallow AI Training、Block on pages with ads、Block 四种。Cloudflare 同时改了 Block 类设置的范围，现在会连 Applebot、Bingbot、Googlebot 这类混合用途爬虫一起拦，因而会影响搜索。站点数据方面，不到 1% 的站点选择拦搜索爬虫，17% 的站点选择拦训练。文中引的 Pew 数据是：超过一半的消费者会读搜索里的 AI 摘要，这些人结束搜索的概率高出 40% 以上；而从 AI 推荐来的消费者，转化率是传统搜索的三到五倍以上。微软的支持时间点列为 2027 年初。
items.summary_en: Cloudflare launched a "Disallow AI Training" setting and an "Accountable" designation for bot operators on 2026-09-15, letting a site stay indexed for search while refusing to let that same crawler train on its content. Its stated diagnosis: the largest organizations run mixed-use crawlers that serve search and training at once, so refusing one means refusing the other, and robots.txt alone can't fix it because it can't identify who is crawling, determine why, or stop a crawler that ignores it. The new Accountable designation requires operators to meet or commit to four things: an AI-training opt-out, an AI-summaries opt-out, URL-level visibility into what was made available for training, and assurance that opting out won't affect search. Apple, Google, and Microsoft all qualify. Controls are now split across three purposes, Search, Training, and Agent, with four settings: Allow, Disallow AI Training, Block on pages with ads, and Block. Cloudflare also changed the Block settings to apply to mixed-use crawlers including Applebot, Bingbot, and Googlebot, which means they now affect search too. On site behavior: less than 1% of sites block search bots, while 17% enable some mechanism to block training. Pew data cited in the post says more than half of consumers read AI summaries in search and are over 40% more likely to end their search as a result, and that AI-referred consumers convert at three to over five times the rate of traditional search. Microsoft's support is targeted for early 2027.
items.why: 选它，因为它把内容被拿去做训练这件一直只能靠喊的事情，变成了三个可以分别设置的开关，而且点出了一个容易被忽略的坑：拦训练的开关改了范围之后，会连带影响搜索收录。任何自己手上有一台站的人，这是今晚花十五分钟就能查清、而且查错的代价很直接的一件事。详见今日行动第二条。
items.why_en: Chosen because it turns "my content is being used for training" from something you could only complain about into three separately configurable switches, and flags an easy-to-miss trap: the blocking settings now reach mixed-use crawlers, so they affect search indexing too. For anyone who runs a site, this is fifteen minutes tonight with a very direct cost for getting it wrong. See today's second action.

items.title: 拍下一张照片这件事本身，也可以有签名
items.title_en: The act of taking a photo can carry a signature too
items.author: Apple 安全研究 · Hacker News
items.summary: Apple 于 2026 年 9 月 15 日发布 Apple Reference Image，一种在 iPhone 上做可验证摄影的选装相机模式。其担保范围写得很窄：证明这是一张真实照片，由 iPhone 相机里的真实传感器在特定时间拍摄。流程分两段，先生成一张安全的数字底片，再把底片冲印成参考图。传感器会重启进一个安全参考模式，在拍摄后立刻对像素数据做密码学签名；帧里嵌入一段 SHA-256 摘要，取自最新时间戳、设备清单和安全启动清单。传感器在出厂时生成 ECDSA P-256 密钥，安全隔区用带 BAA 认证的密钥，时间戳用 RFC 3161 令牌、以 ECDSA P-256 对 SHA-256 签名并给出时间上下界。冲印环节由 PCC 负责去马赛克、色调映射和压缩，用一个神经网络算出置信度分数，再用 RSA-3072 与 ML-DSA-87 组合的后量子签名签出。撤销用照片 GUID 加传感器 ID；底片以 DNG 保存，自动移入已删除照片，30 天后清除。首发机型是 iPhone 18 Pro 与 iPhone 18 Pro Max 的主摄。文章把 C2PA 那类方案作为对照，说它是在拍摄之后附加来源信息，只认证从那一刻起的编辑历史，在编辑链的任何一个环节都可能被攻破。评论区最集中的反驳是翻拍：把 PS 或 AI 生成的图放到高分辨率屏幕上，再用 iPhone 18 Pro 拍这块屏幕，得到的依然是一张有效的参考图，有人开玩笑说很期待看到苹果认证的 UFO 照片。也有人搬出索尼的同类方案，说它内建了景深信息；还有人指出一份专利的权利要求 7 描述了用深度传感器参与图像认证，而 iPhone 18 Pro 恰好有激光雷达。
items.summary_en: Apple published Apple Reference Image on 2026-09-15, an opt-in camera mode for verifiable photography on iPhone. Its guarantee is drawn narrowly: to prove this is a real photograph, captured by a real sensor in an iPhone camera at a specific time. The process has two phases, creating a secure digital negative and then developing it into a reference image. The sensor reboots into a secure reference mode and cryptographically signs pixel data immediately after capture; a SHA-256 digest derived from the latest timestamp, device manifest, and secure boot manifest is embedded in the frame. The sensor creates ECDSA P-256 keys at manufacturing, the Secure Enclave uses BAA-attested keys, and timestamping uses an RFC 3161 token signed with ECDSA P-256 over SHA-256 with lower and upper time bounds. Development runs on PCC, which handles demosaicing, tone mapping, and compression, computes a confidence score with a neural network, and signs with a composite post-quantum signature combining RSA-3072 and ML-DSA-87. Revocation uses the photo GUID plus sensor ID; negatives are stored as DNG and auto-moved to deleted photos, purged after 30 days. It debuts on the main camera sensor of iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. The post contrasts C2PA-style approaches, which attach provenance metadata after capture and certify only the edit history from that point forward, leaving them vulnerable at any point in the editing chain. The dominant objection in the comments is replay: display a Photoshop or AI-generated image on a high-resolution monitor, photograph that monitor with an iPhone 18 Pro, and you still get a valid reference image, prompting jokes about looking forward to Apple-verified UFO photos. Others bring up Sony's comparable system, which builds in depth information, and point to a patent whose claim 7 describes using depth sensors in image authentication, which matters because the iPhone 18 Pro has LiDAR.
items.why: 选它，因为它是一个把担保范围主动收窄、然后说清楚收窄到哪的正面样本：它不担保照片里的事真的发生过，只担保像素出自哪颗传感器、在什么时间。对任何在设计可信度功能的人，这是比 C2PA 那套更有参考价值的一种思路。同时评论区的翻拍反驳也说明，收窄之后如果对外说法不跟着收窄，剩下的那点担保根本兜不住。
items.why_en: Chosen because it's a clean example of deliberately narrowing a guarantee and then stating exactly how far it reaches: it does not vouch that what's in the photo really happened, only which sensor the pixels came off and when. For anyone designing a trust feature, that's a more useful model than the C2PA approach. The replay objection in the comments is the other half of the lesson: once you narrow the guarantee, if the outward claim doesn't narrow with it, what's left can't carry the weight.

items.title: 测了 21 组模型配壳，14 组里只有 1 组差异站得住
items.title_en: Tested 21 model-harness pairs, only 1 of 14 comparisons held up
items.author: HarnessTax · Hacker News
items.summary: 两位独立研究者搭了个 HarnessTax 网站，2026-09-16 上线一套评测：取 7 个模型（Claude Fable 5、Claude Opus 4.8、Claude Sonnet 4.6、Claude Haiku 4.5、GPT-5.6 Sol、GPT-5.6 Luna、Kimi K3），各配 Claude Code、Codex CLI、Pi 三种壳，在 SWE-bench Lite 和 Terminal-Bench 2.0 上跑，以 Pi 为基准。SWE-bench Lite 上，每个模型分别比较配 Claude Code 与配 Pi、配 Codex 与配 Pi，共 14 组配对，30 个任务跑三轮，用 Holm 校正控制多重比较。14 组里只有 1 组差异经得住检验：Claude Opus 4.8 配 Codex 比配 Pi 高 6.7 个百分点，是唯一 clear 的结果。其余 13 组，包括几组 Claude Code 看似比 Pi 高 2 到 4 个百分点的，校正后都跟噪声分不开，其中 Claude Haiku 4.5 配 Claude Code 反而比配 Pi 低 7.8 个百分点。页面自己写道，你的 Claude 模型可能根本不需要 Claude Code。评论区有人质疑，这把壳和 agent 两个概念混了，执行方式、能否委派给其他模型这些变量都没算进去；也有人说，把护栏和安全机制拿掉才算得出税，这是把不安全的成本转嫁成了外部性。
items.summary_en: HarnessTax, a site put up by two independent researchers on 2026-09-16, ran an evaluation: 7 models (Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Luna, Kimi K3), each paired with three harnesses, Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Pi, tested on SWE-bench Lite and Terminal-Bench 2.0 with Pi as the baseline. On SWE-bench Lite, each model was compared Claude-Code-vs-Pi and Codex-vs-Pi, 14 paired comparisons total, 30 tasks over three repetitions, with Holm correction for multiple comparisons. Of the 14, only one difference survived: Claude Opus 4.8 with Codex beat Pi by 6.7 percentage points, the sole result marked "clear." The other 13, including several where Claude Code appeared to add 2-4 points over Pi, were statistically indistinguishable from noise after correction, with Claude Haiku 4.5 on Claude Code even scoring 7.8 points lower than on Pi. The site's own framing: "your Claude models may not need Claude Code." Commenters pushed back that this conflates "harness" with "agent" and leaves out variables like execution pattern and delegation to other models; others argued that stripping out guardrails and safety layers to compute a "tax" just externalizes the cost of insecurity.
items.why: 选它，因为这是今晚唯一一条真做了统计检验的壳值不值评测，结果和多数人的直觉相反：换壳这件事，在他们测的这组任务上，14 次里 13 次都只是噪声。靠某个特定 coding agent 壳吃饭、或者天天切换 Claude Code、Codex 及其他壳的人，这条比任何一篇哪个 agent 更好的评测文章都更值得认真看一眼。
items.why_en: Chosen because it's the one evaluation tonight that actually ran a statistical test on whether the harness matters, and the result cuts against most people's intuition: on the tasks they tested, 13 of 14 harness comparisons were just noise. For anyone whose workflow depends on a specific coding-agent harness, or who switches between Claude Code, Codex, and others daily, this is worth more than any "which agent is better" writeup.
items.flag: 样本量有限：每组比较只跑了 30 个任务、三轮重复，且只测了 SWE-bench Lite 和 Terminal-Bench 2.0 两个基准，结论不能直接推广到所有编程任务。
items.flag_en: Sample size is limited: each comparison covers only 30 tasks over three repetitions, and only two benchmarks (SWE-bench Lite and Terminal-Bench 2.0) were tested, so the finding shouldn't be generalized to all coding tasks.

items.title: 训练过程直播，小米把强化学习仪表盘公开了
items.title_en: Xiaomi live-streams its RL training dashboard
items.author: Xiaomi · Hacker News
items.summary: 小米 2026-09-16 上线 mimo.xiaomi.com/rl，实时展示 mimo-v2.6-pro 和 mimo-v2.6-flash 两个模型强化学习训练的过程指标，页面自己称直接取自训练器日志。页面分总览、指标、关于三个视图，训练过程中持续更新，不是训练完之后补发的技术报告。评论区有人说，没想到这轮强化学习用的训练数据有三分之二是源代码；也有人纠正，这只是强化学习阶段的数据、不是预训练阶段的，现在主流预训练数据里代码本来就占三到五成。讨论最集中的一点是为什么其他实验室不这么做：一种猜测是同行能从训练时长、速度、处理的 token 数反推出模型规模，公开等于把底牌亮给对手；也有人说，对小米这种品牌来说，营销上的边际收益比对 OpenAI、Anthropic 更大。帖子拿到 236 赞、58 条评论。
items.summary_en: Xiaomi launched mimo.xiaomi.com/rl on 2026-09-16, a live dashboard showing reinforcement-learning training metrics for its mimo-v2.6-pro and mimo-v2.6-flash models, with the page describing itself as pulled "live from the trainer's logs." It has three views, overview, metrics, and about, and updates continuously during training rather than shipping as a post-hoc technical report. In the comments, one person was surprised that two-thirds of the (RL-stage) training data is source code; another corrected that this applies only to the RL run, not pretraining, and that mainstream pretraining mixes already run 30-50% code. The most debated question was why other labs don't do this: one theory is that competitors can back out model size from training duration, speed, and tokens processed, so publishing it hands rivals real information; another argued the marketing upside is simply bigger for a brand like Xiaomi than for OpenAI or Anthropic. The post drew 236 points and 58 comments.
items.why: 选它，因为它是今晚训练透明度这条线索唯一的正面案例：把训练过程实时挂出来，而不是等结果出来再挑好看的数字发通稿。对比西方几家实验室一律只发事后技术报告的做法，这提供了另一种可能，也说明要不要公开更多是商业判断，不是技术门槛。
items.why_en: Chosen because it's tonight's one positive case on training transparency: putting the process itself on a live feed instead of waiting for results and cherry-picking the numbers for a press release. Set against Western labs' uniform habit of only publishing after-the-fact technical reports, it's a working counter-example, and the HN debate over motive shows the choice is a business call, not a technical barrier.

items.title: ChatGPT 的下一步广告：点进去不是官网，是跟品牌 agent 说话
items.title_en: ChatGPT's next ad format: clicking opens a brand agent, not a website
items.author: Krystal Scanlon · Digiday · TLDR AI
items.summary: Digiday 记者 Krystal Scanlon 2026 年 9 月 14 日报道，OpenAI 已向部分客户展示了一种专为 ChatGPT 设计的新广告形式：用户点「和品牌聊聊」这类按钮，不会被送出到品牌的网站，而是留在 ChatGPT 内进入一段与品牌自有 AI agent 的对话。Digiday 通过一段视频看到了这个形式。它和现在免费版与 Go 版回答下方那些基础广告位的区别就在这里：广告本身成了与品牌 agent 对话的入口。Wayfair 正在试用，其付费媒体总监 Morgan Brown 把它称作「OpenAI 的 Sponsored Agent 试点」，说这家零售商正以有限规模测试，并在商品准确性、透明度和转人工上有护栏。参与广告主数量未披露。时间线上，OpenAI 首席财务官 Sarah Friar 在 9 月 8 日高盛 Communacopia 大会上说，当前的广告形式只是「基础的起点」，并称已经能看到更原生于 AI 的形式的「早期迹象」，原话是「这些都发生在真正推出一款让人觉得属于 AI 的广告形式之前」。业内看法分两派：Accuracast 集团 CEO Farhad Divecha 类比 Meta 那种把人导进 WhatsApp 的广告，认为这能打开沟通渠道并筛选出需要销售或客服的人；Zeno Group 的付费媒体高级副总裁 Shamsul Chowdhury 说 ChatGPT 广告「对大多数广告主来说回报一直没跟上」，并指出零售商真正想留住的是自己站上的用户数据。报道发布在假日购物季之前。
items.summary_en: Digiday's Krystal Scanlon reported on 2026-09-14 that OpenAI has shown select clients a new ad format built specifically for ChatGPT: instead of being sent out to the brand's website, a click on a call-to-action like "Chat with us" keeps the user inside ChatGPT for a conversation with the brand's own AI agent. Digiday viewed the format via video. That's the difference from the basic ad slots currently served beneath answers on the free and Go plans, where the ad is a link out. Wayfair is trialing it; its director of paid media, Morgan Brown, called it "OpenAI's Sponsored Agent pilot" and said the retailer is testing at limited scale with guardrails around product accuracy, transparency, and service handoffs. The number of advertisers with access is unclear. On timing, OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar said at Goldman Sachs' Communacopia conference on September 8 that the current ads are the "basic starting point" and that the company is already seeing "early indications" of a more AI-native format, adding "this is all before we've really launched a format that feels truly endemic to AI." Industry reaction splits: Accuracast group CEO Farhad Divecha likens it to Meta ads that route people into WhatsApp, seeing a way to open a channel and qualify who needs sales or support, while Zeno Group svp of paid media Shamsul Chowdhury says ROI on ChatGPT ads "just hasn't been there for the most part" and notes retailers want the user data that lives on their own properties. The story runs ahead of the holiday shopping season.
items.why: 选它，因为这是目前最清楚的一个信号：广告的落点正在从落地页搬到对话里。对任何做产品、做增长或者做商业化的人，值得想的不是要不要投这个位，而是当用户的第一个接触点变成跟一个 agent 说话，你的产品里哪一句话、哪一个动作是留给这个 agent 看的。这一层现在几乎没人做。
items.why_en: Chosen because it's the clearest signal yet that the destination of an ad is moving from a landing page into a conversation. For anyone working on product, growth, or monetization, the question isn't whether to buy this inventory but what changes when a user's first touchpoint is talking to an agent: which sentence and which action inside your product is meant for that agent to read. Almost nobody has built that layer yet.

items.title: 换的是训练环境，不是模型：游戏里学到的能力怎么带出来
items.title_en: Change the training environment, not the model
items.author: Alex Duffy · Good Start Labs · Latent Space
items.author_en: Alex Duffy · Good Start Labs · Latent Space
items.summary: Latent Space 的 Richard MacManus 采访了 Good Start Labs 联合创始人兼 CEO Alex Duffy，联合创始人是 Tyler Marques。公司把游戏改造成 AI 模型的训练环境和强化学习数据，客户以前沿实验室为主，卖两样东西：agent 玩游戏的轨迹数据，以及为游戏发行商做的定制数据，同时用游戏专项模型蒸馏一个通用模型。公司 2025 年 10 月从 Every 拆分出来，融资 360 万美元，投资方是 General Catalyst、Inovia、Every 和天使。核心实验是拿一个 30B 模型去玩《1830：铁路与强盗大亨》，再把同一个模型放到金融研究任务上测。两种训练设计都提升了游戏内表现，但只有多轮终端 agent，会用工具探索环境、制定策略、实时调整这一种，同时提升了 Finance-Agent 基准的成绩。Duffy 的原话是你设计这个环境的方式，完全改变了模型能学到什么，并说同一个游戏可以用不同方式切入，看图学的模型和读自然文本学的模型学到的东西不一样。他还提到更新的模型（Claude Fable 5.1、GPT-6 Astra）确实更会玩，但在背叛、协作、心智理论这些性格轴上各家分歧明显；2026 年 8 月更新的 LOL-Alignment 基准里，Astra 与人类评委的一致率是 50%，比 GPT-4o 高 2 个百分点。他的结论是带保留的是：有些游戏技能确实能迁移到现实工作，但广度和可靠性还没有答案。
items.summary_en: Latent Space's Richard MacManus interviewed Alex Duffy, co-founder and CEO of Good Start Labs; Tyler Marques is the co-founder. The company turns games into training environments and RL data for AI models, selling mainly to frontier labs: trajectories of agents playing games, plus custom data for game publishers, while distilling a general model from game-specific expert models. It spun out of Every in October 2025 with $3.6 million from General Catalyst, Inovia, Every, and angels. The central experiment took a 30B model into 1830: The Game of Railroads and Robber Barons and then tested the same model on financial research tasks. Both training designs improved in-game performance, but only the "multi-turn terminal agent that uses tools to explore its environment, plan a strategy, and adapt in real time" also improved results on the Finance-Agent benchmark. Duffy's line is "how you design that totally changes what the model can learn," adding that the same game can be approached different ways, and a model looking at pictures learns different things than one reading natural text. He also notes newer models (Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra) are better at the games but diverge sharply on personality axes like betrayal, collaboration, and theory of mind; on the August 2026 update to the LOL-Alignment benchmark, Astra matched a human judge 50% of the time, 2 points ahead of GPT-4o. His answer to the title question is a qualified yes: some game skills do transfer to real-world work, but breadth and reliability remain open.
items.why: 选它，因为这条把换个更强的模型换成了改你让它练习的环境，而且给了一个很干净的对照实验：同一个模型、同一个游戏，只有带工具的多轮 agent 那种训练设计把能力带到了游戏之外。对任何在调 agent、写评测或者设计训练任务的人，这意味着值得动的变量往往在环境那一侧，不在模型那一侧。
items.why_en: Chosen because it swaps "use a stronger model" for "change the environment you let it practice in," and backs it with a clean controlled result: same model, same game, and only the tool-using multi-turn agent design carried the ability outside the game. For anyone tuning an agent, writing evals, or designing training tasks, this says the variable worth moving is usually on the environment side, not the model side.

items.title: Siri 可能不再是一个模型，而是一个模型调度器
items.title_en: Siri may stop being a model and become a model router
items.author: MacRumors · TLDR AI
items.summary: MacRumors 2026-09-14 报道，代号 pdfu 的开发者从 iOS 27 和 macOS Golden Gate 的私有框架里挖出了两套协议，显示 Siri 的架构支持把第三方 AI 模型接得很深。第一套叫 Model Delegation，接上之后 Claude 会以 Siri 扩展的形式出现，和现有的 ChatGPT 扩展一样，用户在搜索或提问栏的 Ask... 菜单里选模型；需要调用苹果系统能力时，Claude 把任务交回给 Siri。第二套在 Model Manager Services 里，是一个推理提供方接口，可以把苹果服务端的 Siri 模型整个替换成别的模型，比如 GPT-5.6：ChatGPT 拿到苹果的 Siri 规划器提示词和工具定义，可以发起执行系统操作的工具调用，最后由 Siri 用自己的界面和声音把答案念出来。目前的限制是 Ask... 还只支持 macOS 27 Golden Gate 候选版本里的 ChatGPT 扩展，Claude 尚未可用，苹果也还没有把模型委托的权限开放给第三方。文中没有苹果的公开回应。
items.summary_en: MacRumors reported on 2026-09-14 that a developer going by pdfu dug two protocols out of private frameworks in iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate showing Siri's architecture supports plugging third-party AI models in deeply. The first, Model Delegation, makes Claude appear as a Siri extension the way the existing ChatGPT extension does, with users picking a model from an "Ask..." menu in the "Search or Ask" bar; when a task needs an Apple system capability, Claude hands it back to Siri. The second lives in "Model Manager Services" as an inference-provider interface that lets Apple's server-side Siri model be replaced wholesale by another model, GPT-5.6 for instance: ChatGPT receives Apple's Siri planner prompt and tool definitions, can make tool calls that perform system actions, and Siri then presents the answer in its own interface and voice. The current limits: "Ask..." only supports the ChatGPT extension in the macOS 27 Golden Gate release candidate, Claude isn't available yet, and Apple hasn't opened the model-delegation entitlement to third parties. The piece carries no public response from Apple.
items.why: 选它，因为如果这套接口真的开放，操作系统就变成了模型的分发渠道，用户不再直接选模型，而是选一个会替你转派的助手。对做 AI 产品的人，这意味着未来要争取的位置可能不是用户直接打开你的应用，而是你的能力被这个转派层选中。同时它也是今天把担保范围写清楚那条线索的另一面：系统能力交给 Siri、模型能力交给别人，这条边界画在哪里决定了谁承担责任。
items.why_en: Chosen because if this interface really opens up, the OS becomes a distribution channel for models, and users stop picking a model in favor of an assistant that dispatches for them. For anyone building an AI product, that means the position worth competing for may stop being "the user opens your app" and become "the dispatch layer picks your capability." It's also the flip side of tonight's thread about stating a guarantee's real width: system capabilities stay with Siri, model capabilities go to someone else, and where that line is drawn decides who owns the failure.

items.title: 给网站定价一分钱一页，作者看着 Claude 真的付了钱
items.title_en: Priced a page at a cent, then watched Claude actually pay it
items.author: Suganthan Mohanadasan · TLDR AI
items.summary: SEO 顾问 Suganthan Mohanadasan 2026-09-15 发博客，讲他从 8 月开始在自己网站上做的一个实验：给每个页面标好价，AI agent 来读，先收到 HTTP 402（Payment Required），要看内容就用 x402 协议付一分钱 USDC，每次抓取都留一条公开的链上交易记录。9 月 15 日这天有五笔付款结清，其中一笔来自作者自己机器上跑的 Claude Code hook，用的是他自己配的钱包。他说清楚了：目前所有付款都来自他自己的 agent，用的还是测试网 USDC，没有真实价值，也没有真的搜索爬虫上门付钱。文章同时提到背景：Google 正在给部分出版商做 AI 贡献试点，按页面对 AI 摘要的贡献付费，但只给出一个月度金额，不解释怎么算的；Search Engine Roundtable 的 Barry Schwartz 9 月 14 日报道了这件事，Digiday 同一天证实了这个项目存在。作者认为这两种模式的差别在于：x402 这条路，网站主自己就能验证有没有真的收到钱；Google 那条路只能等对方给数字。
items.summary_en: SEO consultant Suganthan Mohanadasan published a blog post on 2026-09-15 describing an experiment he's run on his own site since August: each page has a price, and when an AI agent tries to read it, it first gets an HTTP 402 (Payment Required); to unlock the content it pays one cent in USDC over the x402 protocol, with a public on-chain receipt for every crawl. On September 15, five payments settled, one of them from a Claude Code hook running on the author's own machine, using a wallet he'd set up himself. He states plainly: every payment so far has come from his own agents, using testnet USDC with no real monetary value, and no actual search crawler has shown up to pay yet. The post also covers the backdrop: Google is running an "AI contribution pilot" that pays some publishers when their pages contribute to AI answers, but only gives a monthly dollar figure with no explanation of how it's calculated; Search Engine Roundtable's Barry Schwartz reported it on September 14, and Digiday confirmed the program the same day. The author's framing: with x402, a site owner can independently verify a payment actually happened; with Google's program, all you get is a number to trust.
items.why: 选它，因为它是今晚少数几条能自己动手复现的技术实验，正好和 Google 那条不透明的「AI 贡献试点」形成对照：一边是你自己能验证的公开链上记录，一边是对方给个数字、你只能信。对做内容或做站的人来说，这是一个具体的、今晚就能去读代码的参照系。要提醒的是：这仍是测试网阶段，加密支付通道涉及真金白银，天生不可逆，agent 花钱没有撤单这个选项。
items.why_en: Chosen because it's one of the few technical experiments tonight you could actually reproduce yourself, and it sits in direct contrast with Google's opaque "AI contribution pilot": one gives you a public, independently verifiable on-chain record, the other hands you a number to trust. For anyone running content or a site, this is a concrete reference to go read the code on tonight. One caution: this is still testnet-stage, and real-money crypto payment channels are irreversible by design once they go live, agent spending has no undo button.

items.title: 4000万美元，给AI agent的行为买一份认证
items.title_en: $40M to certify AI agents behave, then insure them
items.author: Rune Kvist · AI Underwriting Company · Latent Space
items.author_en: Rune Kvist · AI Underwriting Company · Latent Space
items.summary: Latent Space Podcast 在 2026-09-16 播出对 AI Underwriting Company（简称 AIU）联合创始人兼 CEO Rune Kvist 的访谈。公司刚完成 4000 万美元 A 轮融资，Ribbit Capital 领投。现有客户包括 Cursor、Harvey、Lovable、11 Labs、Sierra、Intercom 的 Fin，团队目前 20 人。Kvist 的路径：2021 年卖掉第一家公司后读到 Kaplan 那篇 scaling laws 论文，直接搬去旧金山，在早期只有约 40 人的 Anthropic 认识了 Dario Amodei。联合创始人 Rajiv 是他未来的姻亲，原是麦肯锡保险业务合伙人，后来加入 METR，参与在模型发布前和 Anthropic、OpenAI 做测试合作，也和英美政府一起工作。AIU 的产品是叫 AIU1 的标准，覆盖 agent 的安全、可靠性六大类别，每季度刷新一次，改动记录全部公开可查。认证分三类要求：技术控制（比如护栏是否真的存在）、测试控制（第三方要真的跑测试，不能只看文件）、政策控制（谁签字负责、怎么和客户沟通）。走完一次认证平均 3 到 10 周，取决于客户底子。拿到认证不是终点：11 Labs 已经买下了「第一份」AI agent 保险保单，由劳合社（Lloyd's of London）承保，AIU1 就是劳合社定价用的风险框架，保单额度、承保范围今年内还会随标准一起更新。目前还没有理赔案例。Kvist 说下一步是往模型层做认证，对接的是政府和实验室之间的信任缺口，类比穆迪之于债券评级、普华永道之于财务审计；他提到 NIST 下属的 CAISI 想做类似的事，但预算规模跟挑战完全不成比例。版权侵权保险目前做不了，因为最想买保险的往往是风险最高的那批客户，逆向选择问题没解。
items.summary_en: Latent Space Podcast published an interview on 2026-09-16 with Rune Kvist, co-founder and CEO of AI Underwriting Company (AIU), which just closed a $40M Series A led by Ribbit Capital. Current customers include Cursor, Harvey, Lovable, 11 Labs, Sierra, and Intercom's Fin; the team is 20 people. Kvist's path: after selling his first company in 2021, he read the Kaplan scaling-laws paper, moved to San Francisco on the spot, and met Dario Amodei at Anthropic when it had roughly 40 people. Co-founder Rajiv, soon to be his brother-in-law, was previously an insurance partner at McKinsey and then joined METR, where he worked on pre-release testing partnerships with Anthropic and OpenAI alongside the US and UK governments. AIU's product is a standard called AIU1, covering six categories of agent security and reliability, refreshed every quarter with a fully public changelog. Certification has three requirement types: technical controls (do the guardrails actually exist), test controls (an independent third party actually runs the tests, not just reviews paperwork), and policy controls (who is accountable, how customers get told). A full certification cycle runs 3-10 weeks depending on how prepared the customer already is. Certification isn't the end point: 11 Labs bought what's described as the first AI-agent insurance policy, underwritten by Lloyd's of London, with AIU1 serving as Lloyd's risk-pricing framework; coverage and limits will update alongside the standard through the year. No claims have been paid out yet. Kvist says the next step is model-level certification, positioned to close the trust gap between governments and labs, comparing the role to Moody's for bond ratings or PwC for financial audits; he cites NIST's CAISI as attempting something similar on the government side but with a budget nowhere near the scale of the problem. Copyright-infringement insurance isn't viable yet because the customers most eager to buy it tend to be the highest-risk ones, an adverse-selection problem AIU hasn't solved.
items.why: 选它，因为它跟昨晚（09-15）拆穿的 AEF-1「三方联署」假新闻正好是一组对照：AEF-1 那条只有一份文件、没有签署凭证；AIU1 这条有钱压着，劳合社承保、每季度公开改动记录、认证流程要真的跑第三方测试，可查、可验证的程度完全不是一个量级。对任何要判断「这个 AI 安全标准是不是唬人」的人，这集播客给了一套具体的检验标准：看有没有钱在后面兜底，看改动记录是不是公开的，看测试是谁跑的。
items.why_en: Chosen because it's a direct contrast to last night's (09-15) debunked AEF-1 "three-way cosign" story: AEF-1 had one document and no signing artifact, while AIU1 has real money behind it, Lloyd's underwriting, a public quarterly changelog, and certification that requires an actual third-party test run, not paperwork review. For anyone trying to judge whether an AI safety standard is real or theater, this episode hands you a concrete checklist: is there money on the line, is the changelog public, and who actually runs the tests.
items.flag: 创始人自述里提到的第二家跟投机构，播客字幕自动转写为「Frost Money」，未能独立核实这个机构名的准确拼写。
items.flag_en: The name of the second co-investor, as auto-transcribed from the episode's captions, is rendered "Frost Money"; this desk could not independently verify the exact spelling of that firm's name.

items.title: 半数网站发了 llms.txt，没有一个 agent 真的去读
items.title_en: Half the sites publish llms.txt, but no agent actually reads it
items.author: Liad Yosef · MCP Apps · AI Engineer 大会
items.author_en: Liad Yosef · MCP Apps · AI Engineer 大会
items.summary: AI Engineer 大会 2026-09-16 放出 Liad Yosef 的演讲。他是 MCP Apps 规范的联合创建者和维护者（Claude、ChatGPT、Copilot 里聊天内嵌 UI 用的都是这套规范），也是研究「agentic web」的公司 Aura 的联合创始人，此前在 Shopify 做过 agentic storefront。他的核心论点：接下来一两年，个人助手会变成访问网络的唯一入口，网站和浏览器会退居幕后，理由是过去二十年互联网把「传达意图」这件事做成了成百上千种不同的 UI，而一个足够好的助手可以把这些 UI 拆成原子能力，直接帮用户完成任务，不需要用户自己去学每个网站的界面。他讲了一个真实的例子：团队给自己产品选分析工具，问 Claude Code 该用什么，Claude Code 推荐了 PostHog 而不是团队用了十年的 Mixpanel，理由是「PostHog 的 MCP 和 API 接得更好」——agent 对品牌没有忠诚度可言。Aura 做了一套「网站是否对 agent 友好」的评测基准（aura.ai），过程中发现一个反直觉的结果：他们测试的网站里接近一半发布了 llms.txt 文件，但没有一个被测的 agent 真的去读它，几乎所有 agent 都直接冲文档页、再冲首页；剩下大约 40% 用到 llms.txt 的 agent，也只是因为文档页里提到了「有个叫 llms.txt 的文件」才顺带去看。他们另做了个叫 Aura Journey 的工具（journey.aura.ai），能把 Claude Code、Vercel 自己的 harness Eve、ChatGPT 在同一个网站上执行同一个任务的路径实时画出来，三者路径差别很大。他最后提到，行业里正在冒出几种发现层标准：Anthropic、OpenAI、Google、MCP、A2A 一起推的 ai-catalog.json，以及「agentic resource discovery」标准，Aura 自己的目录站已经按这套标准把扫描过的网站整理成可查询的形式。
items.summary_en: AI Engineer conference published a talk by Liad Yosef on 2026-09-16. He is co-creator and maintainer of the MCP Apps spec (the layer behind chat-embedded UI in Claude, ChatGPT, and Copilot) and co-founder of Aura, a research lab for the agentic web; he previously built agentic storefronts at Shopify. His core argument: over the next year or two, personal assistants become the sole entry point to the web, with websites and browsers receding, because the internet spent two decades building hundreds of different UIs just to convey user intent, and a good enough assistant can break those UIs into atomic capabilities and complete the task directly, no learning-a-new-interface required. He gave a real example: when his team picked an analytics tool for their own product, Claude Code recommended PostHog over Mixpanel, which the team had used for a decade, because "PostHog has better MCP and API integration" — agents carry no brand loyalty. Aura built a benchmark for how agent-ready a website is (aura.ai), and hit a counterintuitive result along the way: nearly half the sites they tested publish an llms.txt file, but none of the agents in their testing actually used it, almost all went straight to the docs page and then the homepage; of the roughly 40% that did touch llms.txt, it was only because the docs page happened to mention a file by that name. They built a second tool, Aura Journey (journey.aura.ai), that traces in real time how Claude Code, Vercel's own harness Eve, and ChatGPT each navigate the same website to complete the same task, and the three paths differ substantially. He closed by noting several discovery-layer standards emerging: ai-catalog.json, backed jointly by Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, MCP, and A2A, and an "agentic resource discovery" standard, with Aura's own directory site already organizing scanned domains into a queryable form under that standard.
items.why: 选它，是因为它给出一个具体、今晚就能验证的反直觉结论：写 llms.txt 这件事，如今近乎自我安慰。谁要是维护着网站，还指望发一个 llms.txt 文件就算对 agent 友好，不妨去查真实流量，别再照抄那份清单式的所谓最佳实践。
items.why_en: Chosen for a concrete, tonight-checkable counterintuitive finding: publishing llms.txt is, right now, mostly a comfort blanket. Anyone maintaining a site who thinks shipping an llms.txt file checks the "agent-ready" box should go look at real traffic instead of copying this checklist best practice.
